title: Unique Paths III
summary: Given an m x n grid with a unique start and end, and some obstacles, calculate the number of paths from start to end that traverse every non-obstacle square exactly once, moving only up, down, left, or right.
statement: Given an m x n grid with a unique start and end, and some obstacles, calculate the number of paths from start to end that traverse every non-obstacle square exactly once, moving only up, down, left, or right.
constraints: Walk orthogonally from 1 to 2 while visiting every non-obstacle square exactly once.
Return the number of valid paths.
hints: This is a Hamiltonian-path count on the walkable grid cells.
Backtrack from the start while counting remaining unvisited cells.
Mark a cell blocked, recurse to unvisited neighbors, restore it, and accept end only when one cell remains.
Mark/restore enforces exactly-once visits while exploring every possible route.
editorial: Mark/restore enforces exactly-once visits while exploring every possible route.

tests.explanation: Exactly two routes cover all eleven walkable squares before reaching the end.
Four Hamiltonian routes cover every square.
